# Juan Pablo García

> AI developer who builds RAG pipelines and multi-agent systems and measures whether they actually work. I've built products end to end as the only developer and run a production dashboard for hundreds of schools. Studying AI Engineering at Universidad de Palermo, after a year as an exchange student at the University of Pennsylvania. Available now for full-time remote roles; based in Argentina (UTC−3), English C2.

## Projects
- [Research agent with its own benchmark](https://garciajp.com/projects/research-agent/): A RAG service, a four-agent research loop and a benchmark that tests whether the loop beats a single LLM call. On 100 multi-hop questions it did: 86% correct against 74%.
- [Retrieval ablation of my RAG pipeline](https://garciajp.com/projects/retrieval-ablation/): Each stage of my RAG service's retrieval measured on 1,008 labeled questions. The biggest gain was a one-line tokenizer fix; fusion only helped once BM25 was fixed, and the reranker took over 95% of query time.
- [Prompt injection lab](https://garciajp.com/projects/agent-injection-lab/): 36 prompt injections planted in a tool-using assistant's documents, against four defenses, alone and combined. A warning cut attacks from 42% to 6%; one fake policy update beat every defense I tested.
- [LoRA vs prompting: how much data fine-tuning needs](https://garciajp.com/projects/lora-vs-prompting/): A 1.5B model fine-tuned with LoRA against a larger model prompted with examples, on the same labeled data. The prompt won by over 20 points at 100 examples; at 2,000 the small model was 2 points behind, within noise.
- [Analytics dashboard for hundreds of schools](https://garciajp.com/projects/schools-analytics-dashboard/): A React and FastAPI dashboard in production, following attendance, performance and risk across hundreds of schools.
- [Chatbots and an outreach pipeline](https://garciajp.com/projects/chatbots-and-outreach/): LLM chatbots that answer from client content, and a pipeline that finds leads and contacts them on WhatsApp.

## Explainers (animated, step by step, with references)
- [How an agent harness works](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-agent-harnesses-work/): An agent is a model plus a harness: everything around it that decides what it sees, what it can do, what it remembers and what you can check afterwards.
- [How agent loops work: the loops around the loop](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-agent-loops-work/): Every agent runs a loop of model calls and tool calls. Loop engineering adds the loops around it: one that checks the work, one that starts runs, one that improves the agent, and rules for when each stops.
- [How agent graphs work: nodes, edges and safe cycles](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-agent-graphs-work/): A graph makes an agent's control flow explicit: steps are nodes, allowed next steps are edges, and shared state moves along them. Here is my research agent drawn as one, and when not to draw one.
- [How prompt injection works, and what actually stops it](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-prompt-injection-works/): I planted 36 injections in a tool-using assistant's documents and measured four defenses, alone and together. A warning in the prompt stopped most of them; one fake policy update beat all of them; the safest designs cost answers.
- [How hybrid search and reranking work, measured on my RAG pipeline](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-hybrid-search-works/): BM25, dense vectors, Reciprocal Rank Fusion and a cross-encoder, one stage at a time, with what each one added on 1,008 labeled questions.
- [How an LLM request is served: prefill, decode and the KV cache](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-llm-inference-works/): Why the first token is slow and the rest stream, what fills GPU memory, and how batching and quantization make serving cheaper.
- [How structured outputs work: constrained decoding](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-structured-outputs-work/): Why “reply in JSON” sometimes fails, how a schema becomes a mask over the model's next-token choices, and why valid JSON can still be wrong.
- [Long context or RAG? What models actually use](https://garciajp.com/writing/long-context-vs-rag/): Million-token windows didn't make retrieval obsolete. Where models lose track of long prompts, what each approach costs, and how to choose.
- [How RLHF works](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-rlhf-works/): Reinforcement learning from human feedback, stage by stage: demonstrations, comparisons, a reward model, PPO with a KL leash, and reward hacking.
- [How DPO works, and when to use it instead of RLHF](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-dpo-works/): Direct Preference Optimization turns RLHF's reward model and RL loop into one loss on preference pairs. The math, the trade-offs and when to choose it.
- [How RAG works](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-rag-works/): Retrieval-augmented generation, step by step: from splitting documents to an answer with sources.
- [How AI agents work](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-ai-agents-work/): An agent is a language model in a loop: plan, call a tool, read the result, decide again.
- [How transformers and attention work](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-transformers-work/): What happens inside a large language model: tokens, embeddings, attention and next-token prediction.
- [How neural networks learn](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-neural-networks-learn/): Forward pass, loss, backpropagation and gradient descent, drawn one step at a time.
- [How embeddings and vector search work](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-vector-search-works/): How meaning becomes coordinates, and how a search finds the closest ones fast.
- [How a web request is served](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-a-web-request-is-served/): Load balancing, caching and the database: the path most web requests take.
- [How fine-tuning with LoRA works](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-lora-fine-tuning-works/): Why LoRA trains a fraction of a percent of the weights and still adapts a model.
- [How diffusion models generate images](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-diffusion-models-work/): Image generators learn to remove noise, then start from pure noise and clean it up step by step.
- [How MCP connects AI apps to tools](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-mcp-works/): The Model Context Protocol, step by step: discovery, tool calls, and why one server works in every app.
- [How database indexes work](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-database-indexes-work/): Why an index turns a full table scan into a few reads, and what it costs on every write.
- [How Docker containers work](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-docker-containers-work/): Dockerfile, layers, caching, containers and registries: how one image runs the same everywhere.
- [How to evaluate an LLM app](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-to-evaluate-llm-apps/): Test cases, scoring, version comparisons and a release gate: measuring quality instead of guessing.

## Articles (measured results)
- [When does LoRA fine-tuning beat a good prompt? I measured the crossover](https://garciajp.com/writing/lora-vs-prompting/): A 1.5B model fine-tuned with LoRA against a larger model prompted with examples, on the same 100, 500 and 2,000 labeled examples. The prompt won easily at 100; at 2,000 the small model was 2 points behind, within noise, at 1/29 of the input.
- [What actually stops prompt injection? I tested four defenses](https://garciajp.com/writing/what-stops-prompt-injection/): I planted 36 injections in the documents a tool-using assistant reads. Undefended, 42% worked; a one-paragraph warning cut that to 6%. One fake policy update beat every defense I tested, and the strongest filter cost the answers.
- [Does hybrid search plus reranking pay for itself? I measured my RAG pipeline](https://garciajp.com/writing/does-hybrid-search-pay-for-itself/): I took my RAG service apart stage by stage on 1,008 labeled questions. The biggest gain was a one-line tokenizer fix, the reranker reorders more than it finds, and hybrid fusion added nothing significant until BM25 was fixed, and even then only at depth 10.
- [Does a four-agent loop beat a single LLM call? I measured it](https://garciajp.com/writing/does-an-agent-beat-a-single-llm-call/): On 100 multi-hop questions, my research agent answered 86% correctly against 74% for one retrieve-and-answer call, at about 6× the calls. Where the gain comes from, where it loses, and what I'd change.

## Other notes
- [How to break down a big problem](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-to-break-down-a-problem/): Split a vague problem into parts that add up to the whole, until each part is small enough to check and fix.
- [How to find the root cause of a problem](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-to-find-the-root-cause/): Ask why, answer with facts, and keep going until you reach a cause you can change, so the problem doesn't come back.
- [How to find what broke by halving](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-to-find-what-broke-by-halving/): When something worked before and doesn't now, test the middle and throw away half the suspects each time.
- [How to find the bottleneck](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-to-find-the-bottleneck/): A process runs only as fast as its slowest step. Find that step, improve it, then look for the next one.
- [How to decide what to fix first](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-to-decide-what-to-fix-first/): Count the problems, sort them, and you usually find a few causes behind most of the trouble.
- [How to solve problems with small experiments](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-to-solve-problems-with-small-experiments/): Guess, test small, measure and adjust. Many cheap loops find a good answer faster than one big plan.
- [How AI is changing software development](https://garciajp.com/writing/how-ai-is-changing-software-development/): From autocomplete to agents that ship whole features: specs, conducting, context and loops, how models run, and keeping agents safe.
